# Bonsoir, non

> Menu bar app for macOS that locks any application behind Touch ID, Apple Watch proximity, or a backup password. Free and open source (MIT). Fork of MakLock with hardened security.

## Links

- Website: https://naosou-3355.github.io/Bonsoirnon_maklock/
- Source code: https://github.com/Naosou-3355/Bonsoirnon_maklock
- Upstream project: https://github.com/dutkiewiczmaciej/MakLock

## What it does

- Shows a full-screen blur overlay when a protected app is launched or brought to the front
- Unlocks with Touch ID, an unlocked Apple Watch on the wrist, or a backup password
- Re-locks apps when you switch away, when the screen locks or sleeps, and when the Watch leaves range
- Optional auto-close of inactive protected apps (hides notifications of messaging apps)
- Covers every connected display

## Security model

- When in doubt, stay locked: an unanswered overlay closes after 60 s but the app stays hidden and locked
- Apple Watch: only the paired Watch is trusted; unknown or stale state counts as locked
- Backup password stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hash (600,000 iterations), escalating lockout after 5 failures
- Removing or disabling a protected app, or turning protection off, requires Touch ID or the macOS password
- Emergency shortcut available in Debug builds only
- No auto-update, no network, no analytics
- Terminal, Finder, Activity Monitor and System Settings can never be locked

## Requirements

- macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later, Apple Silicon or Intel
- Built from source with Xcode (no prebuilt release yet)

## Technical

- Swift, SwiftUI + AppKit, menu bar app (LSUIElement)
- Dependency: HotKey (SPM)
